findings.excerpt: A different backup capability or a smaller admissible safe operating region is needed
findings.issue: Shrinking the operating region is presented as a possible remedy although no nonempty finite-clearance robust invariant region exists for the failed drive.
findings.reason: With u(t)<=0 and the permitted constant w(t)=-0.1, d(t)<=d(0)-0.1t. Every finite initial clearance crosses zero eventually, regardless of a smaller region or faster sampling. The one-step feasibility threshold 0.05 is correct but is not recursive viability.
findings.concrete_fix: Replace the final sentence with: A backup capable of moving away from the boundary is needed for an indefinite guarantee. With this failed drive, only a finite operating horizon before clearance is exhausted can be covered; faster sampling or restricting initial clearances cannot restore infinite-horizon robust viability.
findings.resolution: Accepted: failed-drive solution now states finite clearance is eventually exhausted under constant worst disturbance, shrinking the region does not fix it, and indefinite operation requires a different backup capability.

findings.excerpt: The largest Euclidean radius for a strict positive certificate is any
findings.issue: Strict-positive certificates on closed balls have an unattained supremum rather than a largest radius.
findings.reason: For every r<0.6/sqrt(5), the minimum gap is positive. At r=0.6/sqrt(5), delta=-0.6 a/||a||^2 attains zero. There is no largest member of the set of certified radii.
findings.concrete_fix: Say: Every Euclidean radius r<0.6/sqrt(5) is certified. The supremum of these radii is 0.6/sqrt(5), but it is not attained under the strict-positive criterion.
findings.resolution: Accepted: score project now says every subcritical radius works and explicitly identifies an unattained supremum for strict positivity on a closed ball.

findings.excerpt: Near one input$x_0$, suppose a certified analysis gives
findings.issue: The domain of the asserted affine identity is not stated, while the conclusion quantifies over whole balls and a box.
findings.reason: An affine identity only in an unspecified neighborhood of x0 does not certify all perturbations in a radius-0.2 ball, a coordinate radius-0.2 box or every radius below 0.6/sqrt(5). A piecewise-affine classifier can change activation pattern outside that neighborhood.
findings.concrete_fix: State explicitly that the displayed identity holds for every perturbation in a domain containing all audited sets, for example ||delta||_infinity<=0.3. Then all radii and the box used here lie inside the stated region. Alternatively make the score map globally affine in this constructed model.
findings.resolution: Accepted: affine identity is asserted uniformly on ||delta||_infinity<=0.3, which contains all audited balls and boxes.

findings.excerpt: A fixed controller may be run on independent test initial conditions sampled from a stated distribution
findings.issue: Independent initial conditions alone do not establish IID failure trials for rollout validation.
findings.reason: Rollout failures also depend on disturbance realizations, any controller randomness and the horizon/protocol. These can be shared or dependent despite independent initial-state draws. The deterministic model elsewhere permits arbitrary bounded disturbance sequences, so the distribution needed by this statistical paragraph should be stated.
findings.concrete_fix: Specify a fixed controller, fixed test horizon and IID complete test scenarios under a stated distribution, including initial conditions, disturbances and any internal randomness. State that a zero-failure bound refers to that entire scenario distribution.
findings.resolution: Accepted: validation warning now fixes controller/horizon and uses IID complete scenarios including initial condition, disturbance realization and controller randomness.

Eventual entry example explicitly assumes independent repetitions.
Remaining-budget recurrence and original-time accounting are correct; bookkeeping is distinguished from a complete feasible policy.
Scaled-ellipse unconstrained and constrained optimizers are correct.
Derivative sign establishes the constrained endpoint optimum.
KKT multipliers and complementarity are correct.
The remainder upper-bound certificate is conditional on a region-wide valid bound.
Failure of a positive upper-bound test is correctly distinguished from actual violation.
Sensor/disturbance/hold calculation certifies the whole interval because its lower bound is affine in time.
Actuator intersection and scalar projection are correct.
Held and continuously updated controls are distinguished.
No future recursive-feasibility conclusion is drawn from one successful solve.
Sensor-age error addition is sound assuming its speed bound holds throughout the delay.
Nominal Lyapunov decrease, invariant physical band and disturbance-dependent neighborhood are correct.
Persistent-error equilibrium disproves a universal zero-convergence claim.
Tube radius, constraint tightening and error allocation are correct.
Mean-square error is correctly distinguished from a uniform state-domain bound.
The rare-error example does not overclaim physical failure from certificate failure.
Wide measurement interval gives a valid conservative certificate.
Action set is nonempty for every valid measurement in [-0.1,10.1], supporting induction.
Discrete-time safety is explicitly distinguished from intersample safety.
Larger-disturbance boundary example proves genuine actuator infeasibility, not just conservatism.
Lipschitz lower envelopes and their unions are correct.
The next query is certified before its own observation is used.
Negative lower bounds are treated as uncertified, not unsafe.
L=0 is handled separately without dividing by zero.
Safety-margin data are distinguished from performance information.
Dual-norm minima, attaining perturbation and box tie are correct subject to an explicit affine-validity domain.
Conformal order statistics k=18 and unavailable k=20 are correct.
Coverage is described as marginal over calibration/test randomness rather than conditional on every input.
Exchangeability and distribution shift are distinguished.
The union-bound joint-success calculation does not assume independence.
Learning sequence and modeling/certification distinction are coherent.
Hypothetical examples are identified as constructed rather than empirical evidence.
New material does not inherit blanket Lean proof coverage.
Definitions of norms, PSD, KKT, CVaR with fractional atoms, viability and invariant tubes are mathematically coherent.
